title: Pavlo Zibrov
summary: Pavlo Mykolaiovich Zibrov is a prominent Ukrainian pop singer and songwriter, recognized as a People's Artist of Ukraine since 1996. He is particularly known for his collaboration on the song 'Khreshchatyk' with Yuriy Rybchynskyi.

sections.heading: Early Life
paragraphs: Pavlo Zibrov was born on 21 June 1957 in the village of Chervone, located in the Nemyriv Raion, which is now part of Haisyn Raion in [[vinnytsia-oblast|Vinnytsia Oblast]]. He was raised in a family with a Russian father, Nikolai Ivanovich, and a [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] mother, Hanna Kyrilivna, who worked as a teacher.

sections.heading: Education
paragraphs: Zibrov's education in music began in 1965 when he enrolled in the [[kyiv|Kyiv]] Lysenko special music boarding school. He later graduated from the orchestra department of the Kiev State Conservatory of Tchaikovsky in 1981, followed by the vocal department in 1992.

sections.heading: Musical Career
paragraphs: From 1986 to 1993, Pavlo Zibrov served as a vocalist for the State Symphony Orchestra of [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. In 1994, he established his own Pavlo Zibrov Theater of Song and began teaching at the department of pop singing at the Kyiv National University of Culture and Arts.

sections.heading: Recognition
paragraphs: Zibrov was honored with the title of People's Artist of Ukraine in 1996, acknowledging his contributions to the [[music-of-ukraine|Ukrainian music]] scene.
